LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Whole Numbers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Whole Numbers. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Where can we use ordering of numbers in real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands in different situations
2. read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words in different situations
3. order numbers up to tens of thousands in different situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Whole Numbers.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Whole Numbers using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Identify place value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value apparatus or place value charts,
2. Identify total value of digits up to hundreds of thousands using place value charts,
3. Read numbers up to hundreds of thousands in symbols from number charts or cards,
4. Read and write numbers up to tens of thousands in words from number charts or cards,
5. Arrange numbers up to tens of thousands in increasing and decreasing order,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where can we use ordering of numbers in real life?
2. Why should we round off numbers?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Whole Numbers is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
